answer: PoA limits Sybil identities by requiring an enclave-generated key and remote attestation that its code matches an approved MRENCLAVE. A hardware-rooted, non-exportable key binds the identity to genuine silicon, so multiplying identities requires purchasing and provisioning physical processors rather than cloning virtual machines. This raises the attack-cost horizon; each attested thread is independently checked, and a karst of copied VM images cannot forge hardware-backed proofs.
